Student union polls in limbo

A year after student union elections returned to four major public universities, students are again uncertain about when they will be able to elect new representatives, as the one-year terms of the unions have expired without any schedules announced for fresh polls.

Arafat Rahaman18 November 2026 · Updated 18 November 2026
18 November 20264 min readThe Daily Star

A year after student union elections returned to four major public universities, students are again uncertain about when they will be able to elect new representatives, as the one-year terms of the unions have expired without any schedules announced for fresh polls. 

Jahangirnagar, Rajshahi and Chittagong universities held elections last year after more than three decades, while Dhaka University held polls after a six-year gap.

Rajshahi University says fresh elections may not be held before next year, while Jahangirnagar University is not considering polls at present. Chittagong University has promised elections within the next three months, while Dhaka University says preparations are under way.

Shibir-backed panels won most central posts at the four universities, although candidates from other platforms secured some key positions.

The elected unions had pledged to address accommodation, transport, healthcare and other student concerns, but their tenures were also marked by allegations of misconduct and partisan activities.

Outgoing student leaders are demanding fresh polls without delay, with some threatening protests. General students, despite reservations about the unions’ performance, also want regular elections.

At Rajshahi University, members of the Rajshahi University Reform Movement staged a sit-in outside the administrative building yesterday, demanding an election schedule for the Rajshahi University Central Students’ Union (Rucsu) and a Senate session.

The demonstration began around 10:00am and was continuing when this report was filed.

Salahuddin Ammar, the organisation’s convener and former Rucsu general secretary, accused the administration of delaying the election without explanation.

“The administration itself can best explain why it is delaying the announcement or what unknown fear is preventing it from doing so,” he said.

The organisation submitted a memorandum to Vice-Chancellor Prof Md Faridul Islam on November 5, demanding an election schedule by November 10 and warning of protests otherwise.

Rucsu’s tenure ended on October 26, but the authorities see little prospect of holding polls this year.

Rucsu Treasurer Prof Setaur Rahman earlier told The Daily Star that constitutional amendments, formation of an election commission and other preparations would take at least three months.

Citing admission tests, he said elections could be held between March and mid-May 2027.

At Dhaka University, the tenure of the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) ended on September 14. Its constitution, however, allows elected representatives to perform routine duties for another 90 days, after which the union would be dissolved if no election is held.

DU Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Prof Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane said hall provosts had consulted active student organisations, and several halls had submitted proposals.

Senior officials would now hold further consultations before fixing an election date, he said.

Ducsu General Secretary SM Farhad said Islami Chhatra Shibir was ready to contest another election and stressed the need for regular polls.

He said they had repeatedly raised the issue with the administration, but the vice-chancellor maintained that elections could not be arranged in haste. Farhad warned of stronger protests if preparations were delayed.

Mubasshir Mahmud Nibir of the Department of Theatre and Performance Studies said the outgoing union had taken some good initiatives but failed to fulfil several promises.

“Ducsu is not a platform for any political group to display its power. It is an institution of the students,” he said, calling for freedom of expression and accountability.

At Jahangirnagar University, the students’ union’s tenure ended on September 18.

Outgoing Jahangirnagar University Central Students’ Union (Jucsu) General Secretary Majharul Islam said they had repeatedly urged the vice-chancellor to announce fresh polls.

“We didn’t get any plan or honest answer from him,” he said.

JU Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Academic) Prof Shamsul Alam said the administration was not considering elections now, as students and teachers were occupied with year-end examinations and admission tests scheduled for January.

At Chittagong University, Vice-Chancellor Prof Mohammad Al-Forkan said the next Chittagong University Central Students’ Union (Cucsu) election would be held within three months of the outgoing committee’s tenure ending on October 23.

“We will hold the next Cucsu election on time,” he said, adding that detailed discussions would begin after the university’s diamond jubilee celebrations on November 18.

Outgoing Cucsu Vice-President Ibrahim Hossain Roni said the authorities had assured them that election-related committees would be formed after the celebrations.

General Secretary Sayeed Bin Habib said regular elections had been among their electoral pledges and warned of renewed demands if the three-month commitment was not honoured.

[Our respective campus correspondents contributed to this report]
